title: Surprise regulatory fine on bank reputation and stock value

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
We will use an Event Study approach to analyze the impact of surprise regulatory fines on bank reputation and stock value. The Event Study method is suitable for this research question because it allows us to measure the abnormal returns around the event window, which captures the market's reaction to the surprise regulatory fine announcement. The key assumption is that the market was not aware of the fine before the announcement, and the abnormal returns during the event window are solely due to the fine.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s17_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns (AR) using the market model
data <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  mutate(est_ret = ret - (beta * mkt_ret)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Define the event window and estimation window
event_window <- c(-1, 1)
estimation_window <- c(-10, -2)

# Calculate cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) for the event window
car <- data %>%
  filter(event_day >= event_window[1] & event_day <= event_window[2]) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(car = sum(est_ret)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate the fine ratio
fine_ratio <- data %>%
  filter(event_day == event_window[1]) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(fine_ratio = fine_ratio) %>%
  ungroup()

# Calculate the difference between CAR and fine ratio
reputational_loss <- car$car - fine_ratio$fine_ratio

# Perform a t-test to check if the reputational loss is significantly different from zero
t_test_result <- t.test(reputational_loss, alternative = "less")

# Print the result
cat("Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR):", mean(car$car), "\n")
cat("Fine Ratio:", mean(fine_ratio$fine_ratio), "\n")
cat("Reputational Loss (CAR - Fine Ratio):", mean(reputational_loss), "\n")
cat("t-test result:", t_test_result$p.value, "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
We expect the Cumulative Abnormal Returns (CAR) to be significantly less than the fine ratio, implying that the surprise regulatory fine announcement generates negative abnormal returns beyond the direct financial cost. This suggests that the fine has a reputational impact on the bank's stock value. The magnitude of the reputational loss is difficult to predict without more information, but we expect it to be negative and statistically significant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with CAR decomposition: financial cost vs. reputational component
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: CAR exceeds fine/mktcap ratio, confirming reputational damage beyond monetary penalty
_ground_truth.main_effect: CAR ≈ −3.5%; reputational component ≈ −1.5% above direct cost
